Transforms endpoint v2

Create and list transform steps attached to pipelines. Transforms process and mutate events in flight before they reach the destination connector. Base URL: https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2.

Create a transform step

POST /v2/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/transforms

Name Type Required Description
typestringYesOne of reshape, filter, or enrich.
configobjectYesType-specific configuration object defining rules, mappings, or fields.
orderintegerNoZero-indexed execution order within the pipeline. Appended to the end if omitted.
create-transform.sh bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines/pl_ingest_orders/transforms \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "reshape",
    "config": {
      "mappings": {
        "id": "payload.order_id",
        "total_price": "payload.amount_cents"
      },
      "remove": ["payload.internal_notes"]
    },
    "order": 0
  }'

List transform steps

GET /v2/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/transforms — returns the ordered list of transform steps configured for the specified pipeline.

Name Type Required Description
cursorstringNoOpaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor.
limitintegerNoMaximum number of transform steps to return per page (default 50, max 100).
transforms-list.json json 
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "tr_7a9f12b",
      "type": "filter",
      "order": 0,
      "config": { "condition": "payload.amount_cents > 0" }
    },
    {
      "id": "tr_8c4e33a",
      "type": "reshape",
      "order": 1,
      "config": {
        "mappings": { "id": "payload.order_id", "total_price": "payload.amount_cents" },
        "remove": ["payload.internal_notes"]
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null,
  "has_more": false
}

Transform types

Godzilla supports three transform types: filter to evaluate conditions and discard unmatched records, reshape to reorganize fields and strip private keys, and enrich to append metadata. For comprehensive examples, see the Transforming events in flight guide.

Sequential execution

Transform steps execute sequentially by order. Each step receives the modified payload from the preceding step. If an event fails a transform step, it is retried and routed according to your error-handling policy.

Webhooks endpoint v2

Subscribe to platform lifecycle events — such as pipeline.completed or connector.error — as outbound HTTP requests to a URL you control. This is the v2 replacement for v1's polling-only status checks; see the Migration guide if you're moving off v1.

Create a webhook subscription

POST /v2/webhooks

Name Type Required Description
urlstringYesHTTPS endpoint Godzilla will POST events to.
eventsarrayYesList of event types to subscribe to, e.g. [\"pipeline.failed\"].

{
  \"id\": \"evt_wh_2091\",
  \"type\": \"pipeline.failed\",
  \"occurred_at\": \"2026-08-18T09:14:02Z\",

Transforming events in flight

As events flow from a source connector to a destination in a pipeline, you can transform them in real time. Transforms allow you to reshape data structures, discard irrelevant records, and enrich events with additional context before they reach storage or downstream consumers.

How transforms work

Transforms run sequentially in the order defined in the pipeline's transforms array. Each step accepts the output of the previous step, modifies or evaluates the event, and passes the result along to the next step. If all transforms succeed, the resulting event is written to the destination connector.

Reshaping event payloads

Use reshape transforms to rename fields, restructure nested payloads, and prune unnecessary data before writing to the destination.

reshape-transform.json json 
{
  \"type\": \"reshape\",
  \"config\": {
    \"mappings\": {
      \"id\": \"payload.order_id\",
      \"total_price\": \"payload.amount_cents\",
      \"customer_email\": \"payload.customer.email\"
    },
    \"remove\": [\"payload.internal_notes\", \"payload.payment_token\"]
  }
}

Filtering events

Filters drop events that do not match specified criteria. Dropped events are cleanly discarded without causing pipeline errors or halting event processing.

filter-transform.json json 
{
  \"type\": \"filter\",
  \"config\": {
    \"condition\": \"payload.status == 'completed' && payload.amount_cents > 0\"
  }
}

Enriching events

Enrichment steps append metadata, compute derived attributes, or inject environment-specific tags into each event payload as it passes through the pipeline.

enrich-transform.json json 
{
  \"type\": \"enrich\",
  \"config\": {
    \"fields\": {
      \"processed_at\": \"$sys.timestamp\",
      \"environment\": \"production\",
      \"region\": \"us-east-1\"
    }
  }
}

Configuring transforms on a pipeline

Provide the list of transform steps when creating or updating a pipeline via the Pipelines endpoint, or manage individual steps via the Transforms endpoint.

pipeline-with-transforms.sh bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\n    \"name\": \"orders-etl-pipeline\",\n    \"source_connector_id\": \"conn_pg_orders\",\n    \"destination_connector_id\": \"conn_snowflake_dw\",\n    \"transforms\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"filter\",\n        \"config\": { \"condition\": \"payload.amount_cents > 0\" }\n      },\n      {\n        \"type\": \"reshape\",\n        \"config\": { \"mappings\": { \"total\": \"payload.amount_cents\" } }\n      },\n      {\n        \"type\": \"enrich\",\n        \"config\": { \"fields\": { \"env\": \"prod\" } }\n      }\n    ]\n  }'
Handling transform errors

If an event fails a transform step due to unexpected formatting or malformed data, Godzilla retries the event according to your retry policy. If retries are exhausted, the event is routed to the dead-letter queue. See Handling errors & retries for details.

Next steps

Learn how to manage failed transformations and drain stalled records in Handling errors & retries, or configure your pipeline's execution timing in Scheduling & triggers.
